title: At the Neighborhood Barber Shop
description: Look around a barber shop through familiar grooming tools, the chair, and the small actions of a haircut.
cardDescription: Look around a barber shop through familiar grooming tools, the chair, and the small actions of a haircut.
focus: This scene uses the ordinary names of grooming tools and shop furnishings. A cutting tool, its preparation material, and a customer’s protective covering have different jobs.
solvingTip: Look for the object’s purpose rather than its size. Use an everyday seat or protective covering to help cross a less familiar grooming term.
words: Person whose trade includes cutting hair and shaving beards
Toothed grooming tool drawn through hair
Leather strip traditionally used to hone a straight shaving blade
Foamy soap preparation used for a traditional shave
Powered hair-cutting tool with moving toothed blades
Bristled grooming tool kept beside a barber's combs
Protective covering draped around a haircut customer
Seat occupied by a customer during a haircut
Reflective surface showing the back or front of a haircut
Paired cutting blades used to shorten hair
To shorten hair by cutting off a small amount
Line dividing hair combed in different directions
To remove facial hair close to the skin
Basin where a barber can wash equipment or hands

answerNotes.BARBER: A barber is a person doing a grooming trade. The clue asks for the worker rather than the place or a tool.
answerNotes.COMB: A comb has teeth that separate or arrange hair. A brush uses bristles instead.
answerNotes.RAZOR: A razor is used for shaving. Scissors cut between two blades, which is a different mechanism.
answerNotes.STROP: A strop is used to maintain a straight razor's edge. The clue names the strip, not the blade itself.
answerNotes.LATHER: Lather is the foamy material. It is different from a brush that may spread it.

title: At the Shoe Repair Counter
description: Discover the parts of a shoe and the materials and tools used by a traditional repairer.
cardDescription: Discover the parts of a shoe and the materials and tools used by a traditional repairer.
focus: The clues separate a shoe’s outer bottom, upper covering, and inner layers. Traditional workshop names appear beside familiar clothing words, with direct definitions for the less common tools.
solvingTip: Use a body location to identify a shoe part. A clue about a worker or a shaping form asks for a different kind of answer from a material.
words: Traditional name for a person who repairs shoes
Outer bottom of a shoe that contacts the ground
Foot-shaped form used in making or repairing a shoe
Pointed hand tool used to pierce holes in leather
Shoe covering above the bottom and around the foot
Raised rear part beneath a shoe
Cord threaded through a shoe's small openings
Animal-hide material used for many traditional shoes
Preparation rubbed on a shoe to improve its finish
One sewn loop joining pieces of shoe material
Inner material covering the inside of a shoe
To restore a worn shoe to usable condition
Bristled tool used to spread or buff shoe polish
Fine strand used for sewing a shoe repair

answerNotes.COBBLER: Cobbler names the repairer here. The same word can name a baked fruit dessert in another setting.
answerNotes.SOLE: The sole is the shoe's bottom. An insole is inside the shoe, while a heel is the raised rear portion.
answerNotes.LAST: A shoemaker's last supports and shapes the work. This noun is different from last meaning final.
answerNotes.AWL: An awl pierces a small hole. Its short name should not be confused with all, which sounds the same.
answerNotes.UPPER: The upper surrounds the foot above the sole. It names a shoe section, not simply a relative height.

title: Outside the Fire Station
description: Identify familiar station vehicles, protective equipment, and the objects used by a fire crew.
cardDescription: Identify familiar station vehicles, protective equipment, and the objects used by a fire crew.
focus: The station scene combines vehicles, protective clothing, and water-supply equipment. A warning sound and the vehicle carrying it have different names.
solvingTip: Look for a vehicle, a wearable item, or a water-related object. Short equipment words help with the longer station terms.
words: Street fixture from which firefighters can draw water
Loud warning device carried by a responding fire vehicle
Runged equipment used by firefighters to reach higher places
Protective headgear worn by a fire crew member
Common name for a fire vehicle equipped to pump water
Flexible water-carrying tube coiled at a fire station
Protective footwear worn by a firefighter
Large movable panel through which a station vehicle exits
Group assigned to work together on a fire vehicle
Ringing signal associated with traditional fire stations
Large road vehicle that can carry fire equipment
Act of bringing a person away from danger
Building where fire crews and their vehicles are based
Signal calling attention to a possible fire

answerNotes.HYDRANT: A hydrant is a water-supply fitting. A hose is the flexible tube connected to convey the water.
answerNotes.SIREN: A siren makes a warning sound. The clue asks for the device rather than the vehicle's engine.
answerNotes.LADDER: A ladder provides a series of rungs. The word names equipment rather than a building's stairs.
answerNotes.HELMET: A helmet covers and protects the head. Boots and other protective garments serve different body locations.
answerNotes.ENGINE: A fire engine is a vehicle in this clue. Engine can also name the power-producing machine inside a vehicle.

title: Waiting at the Bus Stop
description: Follow a local bus journey through route information, boarding places, and familiar fare words.
cardDescription: Follow a local bus journey through route information, boarding places, and familiar fare words.
focus: This scene uses common American bus-travel language. A route is a course, a fare is a charge, and a transfer connects parts of a journey; actual systems can handle tickets differently.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for information, a payment, a person, or a place to wait. The travel context selects the meaning of several ordinary words.
words: Pass or permission allowing a rider to change to another bus
Charge paid for a ride on a public bus
Covered waiting structure at some bus stops
Raised roadside edge beside a bus boarding area
Planned course followed by a local bus
Large road vehicle carrying passengers along a public route
Designated place where a public bus picks up riders
Paper or electronic record authorizing a bus ride
Published list of planned bus departure times
Person operating a local passenger bus
Individual sitting place aboard a bus
Passage between seating rows inside a bus
Sloping boarding aid fitted to some passenger buses
Route arrangement that returns around a circuit

answerNotes.TRANSFER: A transfer connects parts of a transit trip. Its format and validity depend on the local system.
answerNotes.FARE: Fare is the travel charge. It sounds like fair but has a different spelling and meaning.
answerNotes.SHELTER: A shelter provides a place to wait out of the weather. Not every bus stop has one.
answerNotes.CURB: Curb is the common American spelling for the roadside edge. Kerb is used in British English.
answerNotes.ROUTE: A route describes the course taken. A schedule or timetable instead describes planned times.

title: At the Corner Newsstand
description: Browse a newspaper through headlines, credited writers, columns, and the objects at a small newsstand.
cardDescription: Browse a newspaper through headlines, credited writers, columns, and the objects at a small newsstand.
focus: The clues distinguish a newspaper’s text and page features from the people preparing it and the objects displaying it. They do not ask about current headlines or named publications.
solvingTip: Look for a page feature, a writer’s credit, or a shop object. Short paper words can help cross the longer newsroom terms.
words: Prominent title above a newspaper story
Printed line identifying a news story's writer
Vertical division of newspaper text, or a recurring signed feature
Person who selects or prepares material for publication
Particular published issue or version of a newspaper
Humorous illustrated strip printed in a newspaper
Word or number challenge appearing in a newspaper section
Short name for a camera image accompanying a news story
One printed side of a newspaper sheet
Reports of recent events printed for readers
To reproduce newspaper words on paper
Small sales structure offering newspapers and magazines
Display frame holding copies of a newspaper
Flat piece of paper making up part of a newspaper

answerNotes.HEADLINE: A headline identifies a story. A byline instead credits the writer.
answerNotes.BYLINE: A byline is an authorship credit. It is different from the story's headline or the paper's overall title.
answerNotes.COLUMN: Column has both a layout meaning and a recurring-feature meaning. The clue names those publishing uses.
answerNotes.EDITOR: An editor helps prepare or select material. The role differs from a vendor selling the finished paper.
answerNotes.EDITION: An edition identifies a version or issue. It is not the stand that displays the paper.
